rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **What it is:** an essay argues, describes, narrates or explains a topic in organised paragraphs. The examiner marks STANCE + STRUCTURE + evidence, not length.  ·  **Universal skeleton:** Introduction (hook + thesis) → Body paragraphs (ONE reason each: topic sentence → explanation → example) → optional counter-argument (acknowledge, then rebut) → Conclusion (restate thesis + consequence).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Four types:** *Argumentative* (clear side, reasons, admit the other side), *Descriptive* (5 senses, spatial order, show-don't-tell), *Narrative* (one incident: setup → conflict → climax → reflection), *Expository* (explain causes/process in numbered factors, no opinion).  ·  **Tense logic:** essays live in PRESENT for general truths; past only inside narrative examples; predictions use will/would.  ·  **Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).
